## Recall · Lectures 2, 3, 4 and 6

a) What is the unit vector of the input (0, 5)?
b) Which angle does atan2 give for the vector (5, 5)?
c) What is (3, −4) · (0, 1)?

::: {.answer}
a) (0, 1)
b) 45°
c) −4
:::

## Activity 1 · Speed, steps and input · 18 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The shuttle flies with the speed 6, and the game moves it by velocity × Δt in every frame.
- Δt is 1/30 s at 30 fps and 1/60 s at 60 fps.
- **Do it:** Find the step per frame at 30 and 60 fps. Which velocity does the input (1, 1) get when it is normalized? And the stick (−3, 4) at the speed 10?
:::

## Check 1 · Speed, steps and input

What are the steps and the velocities?

::: {.reveal}
1. The step is 0.2 at 30 fps and 0.1 at 60 fps, so the shuttle flies 6 units in one second at both rates.
2. Without normalizing, (6, 6) is too fast; normalized, the velocity is about (4.3, 4.3).
3. The stick (−3, 4) has the length 5, so the velocity is (−0.6, 0.8) × 10 = (−6, 8).
:::

## Activity 2 · Facing and bouncing · 18 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The game turns the sprite by the angle atan2(v~y~, v~x~).
- At a wall, the part into the wall turns around, and the part along the wall stays.
- **Do it:** Find the facing angles of (0, −2), (4, −4) and (−3, −3). Bounce (4, −3) on the floor and (−5, 1) on the left wall.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/bounce.png)
:::
::::

## Check 2 · Facing and bouncing

Where does the shuttle face, and where does it go after the walls?

::: {.reveal}
1. The facing angles are −90°, −45° and −135°.
2. On the floor, v · n̂ = −3, so (4, −3) becomes (4, 3) and the shuttle moves up.
3. On the left wall, v · n̂ = −5, so (−5, 1) becomes (5, 1).
:::

## Activity 3 · Local to world · 18 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The nose of the shuttle is at (1, 0) in its own coordinates.
- The game scales first, then rotates, then moves.
- **Do it:** Find the nose with scale 2, angle 90° and position (5, 3). Then play Pilot Check.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/sprite-trs.png)
:::

## Check 3 · Local to world

Where is the nose in the world?

::: {.reveal}
1. Scaling gives (2, 0), and rotating by 90° gives (0, 2).
2. Moving by (5, 3) gives the world point (5, 5).
3. Pilot Check expects 0.2, a normalized (1, 1), 135°, 2° per frame, (3, 2) and (4, 4).
:::

## Wrap-up

- You can move a game object at the same speed on every computer and in every direction.
- You can turn a sprite to face its velocity and bounce it off a wall.
- You can draw a sprite in the world with scale, rotation and position.
